title: Primary and secondary research

draft.title: Primary and secondary research
card: The researcher collects new information first-hand, for their own question. A survey the researcher designs and hands out is an example.
The researcher uses information that others have already gathered. Examples are census results, news reports and published studies.
What matters is who collected the information and why. The same document can be primary for one researcher and secondary for another.
Primary research can fit the question closely, but it takes time to carry out. Secondary research is often quicker, but it was gathered for someone else's purpose.
draft.remember: Primary means you collect it yourself. Secondary means you use what someone else collected.

opts: Using a published report on youth volunteering rates
Interviewing ten students about how they use social media
Handing out a survey on part-time work to Year 11
Watching how students mix in the school canteen
a.why: A published report holds information that other people gathered earlier, so the researcher is only using it. The other three have the researcher collecting new information first-hand, which is primary research.
a.clue: Who collected the information in the first place?

b.q: Priya wants to know how teenagers in Penrith spend their weekends. She reads a council report that surveyed local teenagers last year, then runs her own focus group of six teenagers. Which statement about her work is correct?
opts: The report is secondary and the focus group is primary
The report is primary and the focus group is secondary
Both are primary, as both are about teenagers in Penrith
Both are secondary, as both come from other people
b.why: The council gathered the report's information for its own purpose, so Priya is using what others collected, which is secondary. She collects the focus group's information herself, which is primary. Both being about Penrith teenagers does not make the report primary.
b.clue: For each source, ask who gathered the information.

a.best: Using a published report on youth volunteering rates

b.best: The report is secondary and the focus group is primary
